reason: This passage from Genesis 41 depicts God (Elohim) actively blessing and elevating Joseph, a Hebrew, to a position of great power and authority in Egypt. God reveals Pharaoh's dreams to Joseph, grants him wisdom and interpretation skills, and positions him as savior-figure to manage the coming famine. Joseph explicitly credits God with these blessings, naming his sons Manasseh ('God has made me forget all my toil') and Ephraim ('God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction'). The text portrays God working providentially through Joseph, even providing foreknowledge of coming hardship so it could be managed. There is no indication of antagonism toward the Hebrew people; rather, the text shows divine favor and care through Joseph's elevation.
